title: Sets: Chapter Introduction
subject: Mathematics
objective: A set is a well-defined collection: anyone can decide whether a thing belongs to it or not. The chapter builds the language of sets that the rest of mathematics uses.

fill.q: A set is a ____ collection of objects.
The objects in a set are called its ____.
A set with no element is the ____ set.
The symbol ∈ is read as "____ to".
The common part of two sets is their ____.

tf.q: "The best cricketers of India" is a set.
tf.explain: "Best" depends on opinion, so it is not well-defined.

tf.q: The months whose names start with J form a set.
The set of natural numbers is finite.
tf.explain: N = {1, 2, 3, …} never ends; it is infinite.

ar.a: {a, e, i, o, u} is a finite set.
ar.r: It has a countable, limited number of elements.
Every collection of objects is a set.
ar.explain: A is true; R is false: only well-defined collections are sets.

mcq.explain: Union collects every element of A or B once.

mcq.q: {x : x is a natural number less than 1} is:
mcq.explain: No natural number is less than 1.

num.q: Write the set of even natural numbers less than 11 in roster form and count its elements.

steps: A ∪ B: all elements of A or B = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}

num.q: Write A = {x : x is a prime number less than 10} in roster form.

short.q: What makes a collection well-defined? Give one example and one non-example.
short.solution: We can decide for certain whether any object belongs to it. Example: months starting with J = {January, June, July}. Non-example: best cricketers (depends on opinion).

short.q: Draw a Venn diagram idea for A ∪ B and A ∩ B in words.
short.solution: Two overlapping circles A and B inside a rectangle (the universal set). A ∪ B is the whole region covered by either circle; A ∩ B is only the overlapping region.

match.explain: Each symbol or example matches one idea from the chapter introduction.
